title: Reincarnated from the Future
text: “H-huh…”
Just then, it looks like Fleon-chan is strolling through the sky from afar, looking in high spirits.
“Go, go! We’re the Melfilo Squad! Evil is rampant in this world—wipe it out with the fist of justice! Everyone’s courage and strength—”

Lately, Fleon-chan has been having a blast working alongside her Finacée and Sakura-chan as a member of Melfilo. By the way, this Rafuemon… it’s just a vague feeling, but I feel like I’ve seen him somewhere before. I seem to recall him being there in the loop where Itsuki had a good time with Fleon-chan. Itsuki, having awakened to justice, was ignoring him, and he seemed to be talking with Riska… Also, I feel like my Father was wearing a very gentle smile while Big Sister looked troubled.
“Ah… aaaah… ugh…”
Itsuki put his hand over his ear and started struggling.

The Assistant scurried off and hid behind a cover so he wouldn’t be found. It seems he doesn’t want to play with Fleon-chan. That’s extremely rude. Weren’t you supposed to be the third Melfilo Saintwindy?
“Come on! Itsuki-kun! Put these earplugs in!”
Itsuki, desperate for any relief, put in the earplugs that looked like fish cakes.
“Oh… that mysterious phantom song has quieted down… and Fleon’s voice doesn’t bother me at all anymore. This is amazing.”

As soon as Itsuki put on the earplugs, he seemed to snap back to his senses and regained his composure. It might seem like a positive development, but considering Fleon-chan, those things are nothing but a nuisance. We should seize those earplugs and destroy them while we still can. Just as I took a step forward, a bullet whizzed past my feet with a “pakuun.”
“Motoyasu-san, please don’t come any closer. I’m sure you’re just trying to take this gadget away. I have a feeling that’s the case.”
“Come on, Motoyasu-kun, that’s going too far.”
“It’s for Fleon-chan’s sake!”
“Whoa! You hit the nail on the head! Motoyasu-kun, let’s call it quits, shall we?”
“But Father! For Fleon-chan to live a happy life, playing with Itsuki is the best thing for her!”
“So that’s how it is! Naofumi, please understand this already. This guy doesn’t care about anyone but you and Filolial!”
“Motoyasu, I’m not sure sacrificing Itsuki for Fleon-chan’s sake is the right thing to do…”
I do think that if it’s for Fleon-chan’s happiness, Itsuki should just wake up to the side of justice! But since my Father is warning me, I’ll have to come up with a plan.
“Anyway, thanks for the help. This solves my problem, too.”
Itsuki looks completely relieved.
“My future descendants had to put up with some trouble, but this was a huge help.”
“So, I guess it’s time to reveal the secret.”
When Rival laughed, everyone around him—including Father—furrowed their brows. Is he about to reveal the secret?
“Fleon isn’t in the original world.”
“You mean the cause is eliminated? Still, in Itsuki’s case, he’d still carry out law enforcement activities, right? Isn’t that just within the margin of error?”
“Well, I suppose you could look at it that way.”
“Something about that doesn’t sit right with me…”
“Well, what about this? You’re coming even in a world where the Bow Hero is dead, aren’t you?”
“No, that would be way too strange.”

“Yeah, you’re right. So that means Itsuki’s descendants aren’t the starting point, right? I mean, I kind of believed the story as it unfolded, but was what you told us this time actually trustworthy?”

Ren and Itsuki fell silent at my father’s words. Hmm, this feeling brings back memories. In the first world, the gaming experience that Ren, Itsuki, and I relied on turned out to be a mistake. In other words, what someone says isn’t necessarily the truth. Just like me back then, even if this golem named Rafu-emon believes what he’s saying is true, we’ll need to investigate whether it’s actually correct.

And this Rafuemon is a complete stranger who just showed up out of nowhere. Just how much can we trust what this guy says? Depending on the situation, we might have to destroy him… Oh? I feel like my Father from the first world told me not to destroy him?
Hmm, I do remember actually hearing that. Where was it, again? I’ll dig deep into my memory to try and recall it.
“What!?”
My fathers took on an eerie air, and this “Rafuemon” let out a strange cry.

“That’s right. Bow Hero, it wasn’t your descendant who sent this Rafuemon here. We told Rafuemon a lie—that he was your descendant—and sent him off. Your descendant hasn’t done anything wrong, and he doesn’t owe any debt.”
Ah, I remember now. That’s the kind of guy who was coming. It was that Magic Golem that the fathers from various worlds—including the one from the first world—had been warning us not to destroy.
“The matter where all our assumptions were turned upside down once we got here.”
“Huh? What do you mean by that!?”
“Whaaaaaat!?”
Not only Itsuki, but even this so-called “Rafuemon” let out a cry of surprise. Oh? So who sent this guy, then?
“That’s not true at all! I came here because Jurei-kun—a descendant of Itsuki-kun—asked me to!”

“It was all part of the plan, so there’s nothing we can do about it. This guy’s creator is a reincarnated person who, in this era, used alchemy to try to survive the Age of Waves in a state of suspended animation. According to Wild Naofumi, he’s in cryosleep.”
“I see. Now that you mention it, this ‘rip-off’ vibe is pretty typical of a reincarnated person.”

“Cold sleep”—that suddenly sounds like something out of sci-fi. But I’ve heard a similar story from the first world, too. In fact, I’ve heard that Itsuki was once put to sleep in a cultivation capsule.
“……Is this what they call being lulled into a false sense of peace?”
“Yeah. Things have been peaceful up until now… We were a little careless. Maybe we should do some tougher training next time.”
“So even when you’re fighting the terror of brainwashing, you can still get complacent from living in peace, huh?”
“Well, even if the brainwashing is scary, the story does end with us saving the world, after all.”
“You two seem to think it wouldn’t be so bad to wake up to the reality of darkness and justice, just a little.”
“That’s not true at all!”
“We wouldn’t get brainwashed just because we were a little complacent from living in peace!”
“A-anyway, Motoyasu and Gaelion will teach us about the loop. So even if we didn’t mean to, I guess we were getting a little complacent.”
With that, my fathers-in-law were satisfied.
“So, why the cryosleep?”

“I don’t really understand what reincarnated people do, but apparently, once he realized there were other reincarnated people stronger than him—and that their factions were large—he decided to sleep until a more favorable era, aiming to strike it rich with his inventions.”

We defeated my Father from the first world and those kinds of people, didn’t we? There are actually quite a few reincarnated individuals sleeping like that. The Crimson Swine itself had schemed to make civilization regress whenever the era changed in this world, so they figured civilization wouldn’t necessarily be more advanced than it is now, or something like that. Itsuki from the first world said, “In other words, since supernatural abilities will have declined in the world 100 years from now, even I’ll be able to dominate, right?”
“Ah… So he knew Takt was a reincarnated person, but figured that if he stayed out in the open, he’d eventually be found and eliminated somewhere, so he’s been hiding and biding his time, I guess?”
“Isn’t that right? Apparently, his plan was to sleep through until an easier era, since he didn’t want to struggle through this troublesome ‘Wave’ era.”
“He’s been hiding using every trick in the book… even though he’d be done for if his location were pinpointed…”
What a hassle this is. Come to think of it, my Father mentioned something before about me likely ending up in the Warring States period or the Three Kingdoms era or something like that.

“Well, given that summoning to another world exists, I can’t exactly rule out the sci-fi scenario of someone coming from the future… But assuming the creator of this Rafuemon is a reincarnated soul, what was their purpose?”
“Well, it’s obvious that whatever reincarnated souls do isn’t anything good.”
My rival approaches Rafuemon, fiddles around in its belly, and then clicks a part right off. Ah, right—it’s a magical golem.
“Hey, wait a minute! Don’t take me apart! What are you going to do with me!?”
“If I don’t do this, things will get even worse. Just stay still, okay? Okay, okay—”
My rival removes the cover and starts rummaging through Rafuemon’s abdomen.

“…Come to think of it, I get why a good-for-nothing kid wouldn’t take apart a robot from the future, but why wouldn’t a rich kid or a straight-A student do it? If you could replicate even just one part, you’d become filthy rich, right?”
“Naofumi-san, that kind of meta talk is just tacky… But still, Gaelion-san, who exactly are you…?”
As the Rival fiddled around, something slipped out with a slurp. It looks like a black, star-shaped device.
“Look, Naofumi and the heroes, check this out.”

When we checked as instructed, it appeared to be a bomb packed with high-density magical explosives. Magic has already been imbued into it, and it’s set up to detonate at any time with an explosion tailored to the caster’s stats.
“What’s this!?”
“A bomb!? Isn’t it just fuel or something?”
“The energy tank is over here.”
Rival tapped another spot lightly, making a soft “knock-knock” sound.

“He was planning to gain the trust of the Bow Hero and Rishia to a certain extent, then take advantage of a moment’s inattention to make this Roughemon blow himself up and kill him. Wild Naofumi said that not considering the fact that changing the past would make him a target himself is just so typical of a reincarnated person.”
“No way… Jurei-kun…”
“Most of your memories are false. In fact, you shouldn’t have a single concrete memory left.”
“U… uu…”

With a ‘click,’ Rival used Magic to suppress and disconnect the wires connected to the bomb. Then, after hurling it as far as he could with all his might, he snapped his fingers. A light as bright as the sun burst into the sky with a ‘whoosh.’
“Even with a magical barrier surrounding it, it’s this powerful. Well, it’s nothing Naofumi and the others couldn’t handle.”
Having finished his explanation, the Rival put the parts Rafuemon had removed back in place and closed the cover.
“The danger’s been eliminated now. There were traps in the other circuitry as well, but I’ve made sure those won’t activate either.”
“That can’t be… uuuu…”
“I can’t fully understand why you’re so down. But since it’s important, I’ll say this. What’s your goal? Why won’t you let the Bow Hero get together with Rishia?”
“My goal is to make Itsuki-kun and his descendants happy…”
“That’s fine. It’s just that the Bow Hero’s happiness wasn’t the same goal as your creator’s. Well then, good luck.”
“Yeah, I’ll do my best.”
Saying that, this Rafu-emon nodded.
“It’s starting to sound like a heartwarming story, but… does that mean I’ll end up taking care of this kid after all? Or maybe this kid will take care of Itsuki?”

“It seems like he’ll be helpful in all sorts of ways, so isn’t that fine?” my Father asked Itsuki. Just then, I noticed that Ren was looking frustrated. It must be because the chances of Itsuki becoming a hero have dropped. We’re on the same page.
“That means she’ll be a burden on my family! And anyway, Gaelion! Your explanation is still incomplete!”

“I know, you know. The creator of this rough draft got completely crushed by the descendant of the Bow Hero in a tech-related battle and couldn’t win a single thing. So he tried to erase the annoying Bow Hero and Rishia—and the very existence of their descendants—to paint a future that suited him.”
“Isn’t that reincarnated person taking a really roundabout way to do things? And the fact that they’re sending him even without Itsuki means it’s not going to work out either way, right?”
“That’s right. Still, if we let him run free, he’s definitely the type who’d at least create an ‘Experience’.”

Reincarnated people—they’re all just a motley crew. That said, it’s certain they possess the technology to send people from the future to the past. As my rival said, they might just create something like an “Experience.”
“What’s that?”
It’s a device in the desert. In the most recent loop, I still clearly remember it being destroyed by Renzou, Itsuki, and Trash after they’d awakened.
“Boasting about strange things is a characteristic of reincarnators. According to Wild Naofumi, ‘He probably had some weird ambition like, “My golem will rule the world!”’”
“I sort of get it, but sort of don’t…”
Well, those guys are just bundles of pride, after all. Plus, they’re pointlessly diverse.

“Well, apparently, with this reincarnator’s technology, they couldn’t time-jump with their physical bodies, so they sent a golem instead. Also, since it was made to self-destruct, there are some pretty sloppy parts to it.”
“I bet that reincarnated person knew about that anime, too… They probably got the idea from Itsuki’s abilities and characteristics. So… what happens to that reincarnated person?”

“It varies by world, but in the first world, Wild Naofumi took a liking to Roughemon, so she let him run free to make sure he didn’t disappear before dealing with him. In this case, Gaelion will time it just right to handle him in the future, so don’t worry.”
“Is that really okay?　Aren’t you looping with Motoyasu-kun?”
“No problem. Gaelion’s loop preserves memories. Even if the Spear Hero jumps to a different loop, it doesn’t mean the current Gaelion is looping. So dealing with him won’t be a problem.”
“Ah… I see.”
“As for Rafuemon’s origin, we created him to resemble Rafu—one of my favorite monsters—and sent him out so that even the famous Ofumi of later years wouldn’t see through him.”
“Me too?”
“Wild Naofumi was quite fond of Rafu. So you can assume I set up a safety net to prevent him from being destroyed right away. Actually, it’s been pretty effective.”

I can sort of remember that. I feel like my Father used to shield this Rafuemon and treat Big Sister with gentle affection, almost as if he were petting her. He’d say things to Filo-tan like, “If you’re going to talk, you’ve got to be this earnest. You should learn from that, Filo,” and Filo-tan would boo him. He mentioned something about his responses being a bit slow, and that he’s deliberately kept himself from having the power to fully grasp the future…
“Naofumi, why don’t you turn this Rafu-emon into Sadi-emon? It’s not too late. I’m sure he’ll turn into an orca.”
